derivation_notes: The parent assumed the instantaneous saturation argument grows linearly with effective interfacial loading. Here that assumption is relaxed so dense filament packing or patchy occupancy makes shielding rise superlinearly with loading, while preserving antisymmetric conservative exchange and zero flux at C1 = C2.
change_summary: The saturation denominator now uses a squared effective loading before the existing crowding correction, producing a later onset but sharper high-loading collapse of exchange. This changes the scored dC1_dt mapping itself, not merely auxiliary trajectories.

assumption_audit.released_assumption: Interfacial loading enters the saturation denominator through a linear contrast factor before the existing quadratic crowding correction.
assumption_audit.mechanism: Dense scalar filaments or patchy interface occupancy can leave low-to-moderate contrast exchange nearly unchanged but make shielding intensify superlinearly once the interface becomes heavily loaded, changing the curvature of conservative flux suppression without adding a new process or violating mass conservation.
assumption_audit.parent_reduction: The parent is recovered by replacing the refined squared loading dependence with the original linear-loading form in the saturation argument.

response_change.parent_relation: At fixed mixing_efficiency and shielding_memory, dC1_dt depends on concentration contrast only through one shared saturation variable proportional to mixing_efficiency*Abs(C2 - C1), giving a single smooth roll-off scale from near-linear exchange to shielded exchange.
response_change.child_relation: Retain the same conservative exchange variables but relax the assumption that shielding grows strictly linearly with loading before quadratic crowding. Use a sharper loading-to-shielding dependence so the target mapping bends little at modest contrast yet collapses faster once interfacial loading becomes high.
response_change.observable_effect: When varying initial contrast while holding parameters and initial auxiliary states fixed, the child predicts similar small-contrast relaxation but a stronger late-onset suppression of |dC1_dt| at high contrast than any single-threshold parent curve.

evolution_contract.activation_condition: Observable when effective interfacial loading (1 + shielding_memory)*mixing_efficiency*Abs(C2 - C1) spans from much less than 1/saturation_contrast to order 1/saturation_contrast or larger during trajectories started from different initial concentration contrasts under the same parameter set.
evolution_contract.train_hidden_contrast: In training, moderate contrasts identify the near-linear and first saturation bend; in holdout, larger reachable contrasts expose whether suppression remains tied to the parent's single loading threshold or steepens disproportionately at high loading.
evolution_contract.continuation_path: Recover the parent by taking the refined shielding nonlinearity back to its linear-loading form, so the effective saturation variable is again proportional to saturation_contrast*(1 + shielding_memory)*mixing_efficiency*Abs(C2 - C1).
evolution_contract.domain_mechanism: superlinear loading-dependent interfacial shielding in conservative tracer exchange
evolution_contract.scientific_mechanism: Dense scalar filaments or patchy interface occupancy can leave low-to-moderate contrast exchange nearly unchanged but make shielding intensify superlinearly once the interface becomes heavily loaded, changing the curvature of conservative flux suppression without adding a new process or violating mass conservation.
evolution_contract.difficulty_rationale: This embedding is harder than a coefficient-only correction because it changes the shape of the loading-to-flux suppression law itself: one shared parameter set in the parent can shift amplitude and threshold but cannot simultaneously preserve weak suppression at moderate loading and produce the steeper high-loading collapse created by the squared loading dependence.
evolution_contract.assumption_before: The saturation/shielding argument is linear in effective interfacial loading.
evolution_contract.assumption_after: The saturation/shielding argument grows superlinearly with effective interfacial loading before the existing crowding correction.
evolution_contract.parent_reduction: The parent is recovered by replacing ((1 + shielding_memory)*mixing_efficiency*Abs(C2 - C1))**2 with (1 + shielding_memory)*mixing_efficiency*Abs(C2 - C1) in the denominator.
evolution_contract.observable_signature: Across trajectories with the same parameter set and the same initial auxiliary states mixing_efficiency(0)=1 and shielding_memory(0)=0, but different initial concentration contrasts, the child keeps dC1_dt close to the unsaturated linear exchange at modest contrast while showing disproportionately stronger suppression once loaded_interface becomes large. The parent can only provide one smooth roll-off tied to a linear loading coordinate, so it cannot match both the mild mid-range bending and the sharper high-contrast collapse in the scored target mapping.
evolution_contract.shortcut_blocked: Refitting all existing parent parameters only rescales the single linear-loading threshold and its crowding strength. That can move the bend earlier or later and alter overall sharpness, but it cannot create the child's specific contrast pattern in which moderate-loading exchange remains comparatively less suppressed while high-loading exchange collapses more strongly under the same parameter set. Because this difference appears directly in dC1_dt as a function of supplied states C1, C2, mixing_efficiency, and shielding_memory, adjusting auxiliary trajectories alone cannot absorb it.

evolution_plan.activation_condition: Observable when effective interfacial loading (1 + shielding_memory)*mixing_efficiency*Abs(C2 - C1) spans from much less than 1/saturation_contrast to order 1/saturation_contrast or larger during trajectories started from different initial concentration contrasts under the same parameter set.
evolution_plan.train_hidden_contrast: In training, moderate contrasts identify the near-linear and first saturation bend; in holdout, larger reachable contrasts expose whether suppression remains tied to the parent's single loading threshold or steepens disproportionately at high loading.
evolution_plan.continuation_path: Recover the parent by taking the refined shielding nonlinearity back to its linear-loading form, so the effective saturation variable is again proportional to saturation_contrast*(1 + shielding_memory)*mixing_efficiency*Abs(C2 - C1).
evolution_plan.gap_statement: The current law assumes that the instantaneous saturation/shielding argument grows linearly with effective loading, so one threshold controls both onset and severity of exchange suppression.
evolution_plan.baseline_assumption: Interfacial loading enters the saturation denominator through a linear contrast factor before the existing quadratic crowding correction.
evolution_plan.scientific_mechanism: Dense scalar filaments or patchy interface occupancy can leave low-to-moderate contrast exchange nearly unchanged but make shielding intensify superlinearly once the interface becomes heavily loaded, changing the curvature of conservative flux suppression without adding a new process or violating mass conservation.
evolution_plan.rationale: A realistic next refinement is to relax the parent's single-threshold saturation assumption rather than add another state. The parent target mapping from observed states to dC1_dt is essentially controlled by one loading coordinate, so after refitting its existing parameters it can shift the overall slope and threshold but still produces one characteristic bend as contrast increases. Vary the initial concentration contrast C1(0)-C2(0) while holding all parameters, mixing_efficiency(0)=1, and shielding_memory(0)=0 fixed. Under admissible conditions with nonnegative concentrations and closed conservative exchange, trajectories from small contrast probe the linear regime, while larger initial contrasts generate higher loaded_interface and stronger shielding memory buildup. A child with superlinear loading-to-shielding dependence changes the target mapping itself: low-contrast dC1_dt remains close to the parent, but high-contrast dC1_dt is more strongly suppressed than the parent can match with one shared parameter set without spoiling the moderate-contrast behavior. This is observable directly in the scored derivative, not only in auxiliary-state trajectories. The refinement remains scientifically admissible because it preserves antisymmetric exchange, zero flux at C1=C2, and stronger damping of contrast at large loading.

scenario_text: A passive dissolved tracer is exchanged between two connected, well-mixed fluid volumes. The concentrations in both volumes evolve jointly as turbulent stirring transports tracer from the more concentrated volume toward the less concentrated one. The benchmark targets the instantaneous concentration-change rate in the first volume. There are no reactions, external tracer sources, or net loss from the two-volume system.
